title: Component catalogue (registry/catalogue.yaml)
description: Every nanoSoC-related repo on both hosts, grouped into components, each with exactly one canonical host. Owner: registry loader. A1, B1, B6, B9. Cross-file rules the loader enforces (not expressible here) are listed in docs/contracts/README.md.

external.description: Third-party repos pinned inside registered trees (e.g. picotcp). Not components: no class, never tested, not counted in A1. Listing one here stops B9 flagging its URL as unknown.

ignored.description: A1: repos in the GitHub org or GitLab group that are NOT nanoSoC-related (other SoC families, demos, org housekeeping). Listed with a reason so the inventory classifies them (role `ignored`) instead of flagging them; never mirrored, walked or tested. A repo may appear in only one section (loader rule 1).

vendor_allowlist.description: CR-6a (D2, D11; David's U1 decision, 2026-10-10): scanner findings the registry owner has judged. Both vendor gates (t0.vendor.no-arm-ip and, CR-6, t0.vendor.no-foundry-data) treat a finding matched by an `allow` entry as clean (recorded as allowed in the item's `why`) and a finding matched by a `warn` entry as WARN (amber: listed, never FAIL, never hidden). A finding no entry matches stays FAIL in the arm gate; in the foundry gate it takes its rule's `foundry_rules` severity (WARN by default). Optional; added without a schema bump (README section 2 rule 4).

foundry_rules.description: CR-6 (the vendor gate split; David 2026-10-13, chat: work autonomously): the severity of a foundry-family scanner rule (every rule but arm.*, file.sha and scan.unscannable: foundry file types, values, site paths, licence servers, big files, and, CR-19 (David 2026-10-14, interactive), the toolkit's ident release/bundle-code rule). t0.vendor.no-foundry-data reports an uncovered finding of a rule listed here with `severity: fail` as FAIL; any other foundry finding is WARN (amber, never FAIL). vendor_allowlist entries still apply first (`allow` clean, `warn` amber). Two entries for one rule: `fail` wins. Optional; added without a schema bump (README section 2 rule 4).

rule.description: The scanner rule id as the scanner reports it (the toolkit's ids may have no dot).

severity.description: `fail`: an uncovered finding of this rule FAILs the gate. `warn`: the default, written down.

rule.description: The scanner rule id the entry covers (e.g. arm.banner). CR-6: the toolkit scanner's ids may have no dot (the dot was required before; loosened, no bump).

match.description: What the entry covers; every key given must hold. `component`: the catalogue component (or external) whose tree holds the file. `path_glob`: fnmatch glob on the file's path inside that tree (`*` crosses `/`). `file_sha`: the blob id of the file, so the entry stops covering a changed file.

severity.description: `allow`: the finding is clean. `warn`: the gate row is WARN and names the item. There is no `block`: an uncovered finding is FAIL already.

canonical.description: A1: the one canonical host. Release tags are made only here (C10).

copies.description: B6: independent repos holding the same history on another host or group. Compared every poll (SAME / AHEAD n / DIVERGED); never assumed to be mirrors.

aliases.description: B9: other names of the SAME repo (host redirects after a move or rename). A pinned URL that resolves to an alias belongs to this component.

known_rewrites.description: B3/B8: default-branch rewrites that happened before the tool watched this repo. A pinned commit listed in `lost` is REWRITTEN, not MISSING. Rewrites seen by the tool itself are recorded as rewrite_alert observations, not here.
